scope: The attended container generation migration of the retained source database sbarbase-durable-db (owner durable-upstream) on the workstation, run once on 2026-09-25 with lab/migrate-generation.py and its explicit --attended-retained --confirm-retained override. Row counts come from two cold copies of the pgdata volume, one before and one after, each restored into a scratch volume and read by a network-less throwaway container; the fenced environment database was opened for counting on those copies only, never on the retained cluster. No production readiness, load or capacity claim.
command: /usr/bin/python3 lab/migrate-generation.py --state .lab/upstream --volume sbarbase-durable-pgdata --network sbarbase-durable-net --tier system.db --inventory-runtime .secrets/upstream/runtime.json --retired stopped --assert-retired-will-not-return --attended-retained --confirm-retained sbarbase-durable-db

preconditions.default_refusal_observed: Retained placement migration is a deliberate operator run; this command refuses it
preconditions.cutover_record: present and unchanged; environment e_60332245e3a0426dd242492f stays exported to the recovery target, fenced on the source and paused in routing

backup.restore_note: The cold volume tar is the faithful backup. The pg_dumpall was taken after allowing connections to the fenced database on the scratch copy, so restoring that dump would make the exported environment connectable again; restore from the tar, or re-fence after a dump restore.

rules.statement: Not byte identical. Every one of the 17 retired rules is kept in its order; 12 rules are added, one studio, realtime and developer login per environment for four environments, which the current inventory builder emits and the next ordinary startup would have published anyway.

readback.note: The tier label and the four per device limits match resource_policy system.db. cpu.weight 174 and io.weight default 100 do not match the mapping RESOURCE-POLICY section 3.1 infers (about 79 for 2048 shares); recorded as observed, not reconciled.

row_counts.method: exact count(*) of every ordinary and partitioned table outside pg_catalog, information_schema and toast, in every non-template database
